name: stray sod (lone sod, fod seachran)

attributes.attribute: an Irish folk motif of an enchanted turf
sets a glamour spell upon a stray sod
causes a passerby to become pixy-led
wanders for hours when struck by the stray sod

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Stray sod is an Irish folk motif. It has two other names, lone sod and fod seachran. The story turns on being led away from your proper road. A fairy sets a glamour spell upon a piece of turf. It puts that enchanted sod on the path, where no one may notice it. The sod can sit hidden even in the middle of a road. When the foot of a passerby touches the sod, all the country round shrugs into an unknown shape. The traveler becomes pixy-led. Lost and confused, the person can wander for hours and grow weak with effort. The mischief ends only when the fairy who set the trap chooses to set the world right. The motif shows how close and how unkind the fairy folk could stand to the ordinary road.
